subject.title: feat: AI safety event taxonomy — plugin emission API and manifest policy

question: Should OpenClaw add a permanent public plugin SDK contract for AI-safety diagnostic events, and if so should it be a host-bound plugin API facade with manifest allowlists and strict runtime validation?
rationale: The choice defines a new security-sensitive and compatibility-sensitive plugin contract; code repair cannot safely decide the API location, trusted-plugin policy, attribution model, or whether the six-type taxonomy is permanent.

options.title: Adopt a host-bound API
options.body: Approve the capability only after moving identity, trust, manifest policy, payload validation, and session attribution behind a loader-constructed plugin API closure.

options.title: Keep diagnostics internal
options.body: Reject the public emission contract and keep AI-safety diagnostics limited to core or bundled owner code until a narrower extension requirement is established.

options.title: Pause for taxonomy design
options.body: Hold this PR and its dependent contract work until the canonical issue defines event ownership, privacy, exporter semantics, and versioning together.

recommendation.title: Adopt a host-bound API
recommendation.body: Approve the capability only after moving identity, trust, manifest policy, payload validation, and session attribution behind a loader-constructed plugin API closure.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant plugin registry, manifest, public API, and browser ownership history most strongly routes this cross-boundary contract decision here.
